subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Biobanks and Research Ethics
description: Learn Biobanks and Research Ethics in one minute.

hook.text: Millions of blood samples sit in freezers across the world. The donors often have no idea their DNA is being studied.

buildup.text: Biobanks store biological samples for medical research — from leftover blood tests to donated tissue.

discovery.text: Henrietta Lacks' cells were taken without consent in 1951 and used in research for decades. Her family learned later.

twist.text: Modern consent forms often include broad permissions. You agree once — your sample is used for research forever.

climax.text: Your biological sample can outlive you and contribute to research you never imagined — or approved.

quiz.question: What happened with Henrietta Lacks' cells?
options: They were taken without consent and used in research for decades
She donated them voluntarily to a specific research project
They were destroyed after initial testing
